title: NSAT General Mock Test 10
description: Complete NSAT General mock test #10 with realistic exam experience. 80 questions across 6 sections.
instructions: Marking scheme: +4 for correct, -1 for incorrect
Answer all questions - no optional sections
Test is proctored via webcam and microphone

questions.questionText: John sold two items for a total of Rs 48,000. By selling one item at a profit of 25% and the other at a loss of 15%, he ensures that the transaction ends with no overall profit or loss. Find the difference between the selling prices of the two items.

There are 525 boxes of candies, 315 boxes of cookies, and 420 boxes of chocolates in a warehouse. The warehouse wants to package them so that there are an equal number of boxes of chocolates, cookies, and sweets in each package. What is the largest number of identical packages they can make?

Two taps, A and B, can fill a water tank in 36 minutes and 48 minutes respectively. Both the taps are opened at the same time, but tap A is turned off after a certain time while tap B remains open. If the tank is to be filled completely in exactly 24 minutes, after how much time should tap A be turned off?
Determine the sum of the digits of the greatest number that gives the same remainder when it divides each of the numbers: 15048, 8548, 8048, and 13548.

Two containers hold mixtures with different percentages of salt. The first container has 6 kg of a salt mixture, and the second has 12 kg. Equal quantities were removed from both mixtures. The quantity taken from the first was added to the second, and the quantity taken from the second was added to the first. After this exchange, both containers ended up with mixtures having the same percentage of salt. What was the weight of the portion taken from each container?

A person covers a distance of 245 km in 5 hours, traveling partially by car and partially by bus. If he had traveled the entire journey by car, he would have saved  ⁠<inlineMath>\frac{3}{5} ⁠</inlineMath> of the time he spent on the bus and would have reached his destination 1.5 hours earlier. How much distance he travelled by bus

A committee consisting of 11 members is to be formed from a group of 8 managers, 6 engineers, 4 analysts, and 2 accountants. However, there is a disagreement between a particular manager and a particular accountant and they refuse to be part of the same committee. What is the number of possible ways to form the committee so that these two persons are not selected together?

Amit and Arjun started their journey together from Delhi to Jaipur. Arjun travels at a speed of 36 km/h, but Amit travels at a speed of 45 km/h. After thirty minutes Vikram also started on the same route from Delhi to Jaipur. After some time, Vikram overtook Arjun and 90 minutes later he overtook Amit. What is the speed of Vikram?
For a 500 km trip, a fast train takes two hours less than a slow train. What are the two trains' speeds if the slow train's speed is 15 km/h less than the fast train's?

Two fixed deposit schemes offered by different banks provide interest rates that differ by 4%. An investment made for one year in the first scheme earns Rs 350 as interest. The same amount invested in the second scheme for one year earns Rs 550 as interest. What are the interest rates offered by the two banks?

A school organized a quiz competition where three students, Amit, Bina, and Chetan, participated. Each of them answered exactly 140 questions, but the total number of distinct questions answered by all three was only 200. A question is considered easy if it was answered by all three students and difficult if it was answered by only one of them. What is the difference between the number of difficult questions and the number of easy questions?
For which of the following range of values of <inlineMath>x</inlineMath>, the inequality <inlineMath>2{x^2} - 5x - 8 \le \left| {2{x^2} + x} \right|</inlineMath> hold true?

In a school, two batches of pencils were being distributed equally among a certain number of students. After distribution, 480 pencils remained undistributed from the first batch and 360 from the second batch. If the remaining pencils in the two batches are combined and then distributed equally among the same number of students, 300 pencils remained undistributed. Find the maximum number of students?
A shopkeeper sells a gadget for Rs 1200 and makes a profit that is 25 times the loss incurred when selling it for Rs 472.At what price should the gadget be sold to ensure a 30% profit?

Neha, Ramesh and Kavita contributed a combined amount of Rs 1,26,000 to launch a start-up. After one year, the venture earns a profit of Rs 75,600. Neha invests her share of the profit in a fixed deposit that offers 10% compound interest per annum, while Ramesh puts his share in a financial scheme that offers 20% compound interest per annum. After 2 years, Neha receives Rs 4,536 as interest from her investment, and Ramesh receives Rs 7,560 as interest after 1 year. Determine how much Kavita initially invested in the business.

A man stands on the shore and pulls in a rope attached to a boat offshore. He pulls the rope in at <inlineMath>2{\rm{ m/s}}</inlineMath>. The boat is 6 meters from the point on the shore directly under the man's hand. How fast is the boat approaching the shore when the rope is 10 m long?

A drawer contains 8 identical black socks, 8 identical white socks, and 1 unique red sock. You draw 3 socks at random without replacement. What is the probability that the red sock is not the first sock (Order matters), and at least one pair drawn is matching in colour?

Also, two of them belong in level 1, one of them belongs in level 2 and one of them belongs in level 3. The departments are sales, marketing, production, and advertising. One of them can work in all the departments while another is weak in all the departments. At a space agency, five suits (1 to 5)  are arranged in a line from left to right. Five astronauts are preparing for missions, each assigned to a different launchpad: Pad A, Pad B, Pad C, Pad D, or Pad E, not necessarily in the same order.

The astronauts—Arjun, Bella, Chen, David, and Elena—are each wearing a uniquely colored spacesuit: red, blue, green, white, or black. 

They are scheduled to launch at different times: 2 AM, 3 AM, 4 AM, 5 AM, or 6 AM, each heading to a distinct mission destination: Mars, Venus, Europa, Titan, or Ganymede

No two astronauts share the same launchpad, suit color, launch time, or mission destination.

  • Arjun launches at 3 AM to the Titan. 
  • The middle suit is black.
  • Bella launches at 6 AM
  • Chen, in a blue suit, is on the left of the Titan mission.
  • To the right of the Mars mission is the one at Pad C.
  • David’s mission is from Pad B
  • A green suit is next to the Europa mission.
  • The Pad C launch is at 2 AM.
  • Elena launches at 4 AM and is to the right of the Pad A mission. 
  • The red suit is for the Pad D launch. 
  • The first suit goes for Venus. 
  • The black suit launches at 5 AM. 
  • The Venus mission is next to the Europa. 
  • Pad D mission launches at 3 AM.

Who goes to Ganymede?

  1. She walks from her bed to the closet (6 meters away) at a speed of 1.5 m/s to get clothes.
  2. Then she walks from the closet to the dresser (4 meters further) at a speed of 2 m/s to put away the clothes.
  3. Finally, she walks back to the bed (a total of 10 meters from the dresser) at 1 m/s.

She rests at the dresser for 30 seconds before returning to the bed.

How much total time does she spend starting from bed and back to bed?
What is the total distance Riya walks?

Indian literature is one of the richest and most diverse literary traditions in the world, spanning thousands of years and multiple languages. From the ancient Vedas, Upanishads, and epics like the Mahabharata and Ramayana to modern works in English, Hindi, and regional languages, Indian literature has evolved while preserving its deep philosophical and cultural roots. Medieval literature saw the rise of Bhakti and Sufi poetry, emphasizing devotion and spirituality, while the colonial era brought forth progressive writers who addressed themes of freedom, social justice, and reform. In contemporary times, Indian authors such as Rabindranath Tagore, R.K. Narayan, Arundhati Roy, and Salman Rushdie have gained international recognition, blending traditional storytelling with modern themes. Indian literature continues to be a dynamic force, reflecting the country's evolving identity, struggles, and aspirations.

In light of the above, which of the following statements best summarises the passage?

options.text: Indian literature has evolved from ancient texts to modern works, reflecting cultural and historical changes.
Indian literature has remained unchanged over time, focusing only on ancient traditions.
Indian literature is limited to religious and spiritual themes without addressing social or political issues.
Indian literature primarily consists of epics like the Mahabharata and Ramayana, with little influence of modern writers.

questions.questionText:
Yoga, a historic Indian practice, is increasingly recognised not just for physical fitness, but also as a powerful therapeutic tool—in particular for youngsters with disabilities. In recent years, educators, therapists, and parents have turned to yoga to assist youngsters dealing with physical, cognitive, and emotional challenges.

Children with conditions like autism, cerebral palsy, ADHD, or developmental delays frequently struggle with motor coordination, attention span, and emotional regulation. Yoga, with its gentle moves, respiratory techniques, and emphasis on mindfulness, gives a non-competitive and adaptable way to help these kids connect to their bodies and minds. For instance, simple poses can enhance stability and flexibility, even as deep respiration facilitates calming anxiety and improving recognition.

Yoga fosters a sense of self-worth and inner peace. In environments in which children frequently face labels or obstacles, yoga encourages self-esteem and personal growth. Group yoga sessions also promote social interaction, empathy, and cooperation without stress or judgment.

When integrated into therapy or school workouts, yoga turns into more than a workout; it becomes a bridge to self-assurance, resilience, and holistic well-being for youngsters with disabilities.

 

Based on the passage, which deeper reason best explains why yoga is considered an effective tool for children with disabilities?

options.text: Yoga mainly targets physical limitations and replaces the need for emotional therapy.
Yoga allows children to become emotionally independent by isolating them from peer influence.
Yoga creates an inclusive space where emotional, physical, and social needs are addressed together without relying on fixed outcomes.
Yoga works only because it has spiritual roots, which make it more powerful than modern therapies.

questions.questionText:
Ethics is frequently seen as a machine of right and wrong, however, psychology indicates that our moral selections are hardly ever merely logical. Instead, they are shaped by emotions, upbringing, social surroundings, and even unconscious biases. People don’t usually comply with moral regulations due to the fact that they understand them; they frequently follow them because they experience remorse while breaking them, or because society rewards certain behaviours. 

Psychologists argue that ethics isn't always only a philosophical idea, but a set of behaviours shaped by cultural values and mental patterns. What’s visible as moral in one society can be judged in a different way in every other. This doesn’t suggest that ethics are meaningless; however, it suggests that information about how human beings behave is essential to constructing a genuinely moral society.
 

Which of the following best summarises the central idea of the passage?

options.text: Ethical behaviour is mostly taught through childhood rules and rarely changes later in life.
Ethical decisions are influenced by personal emotions, social settings, and cultural values, not just logic or universal rules.
Ethics is a fixed set of principles agreed upon by all societies and enforced by psychological pressure.
People follow ethics only because they fear punishment or judgment by others in society.

questions.questionText:
Technology has revolutionised contemporary education, transforming how college students study and teachers instruct. Integrating digital equipment, online infrastructure, and artificial intelligence has made education more handy, interactive, and personalised. Online learning platforms, including video lectures and digital classrooms, allow college students to study from anywhere, breaking down traditional limitations to training.

However, the upward thrust of an era in training also gives way to demanding situations. Increased screen time, digital distractions, and the digital divide (the space between those with and without access to technology) can affect learning experiences. While technology has uplifted schooling in many ways, it's crucial to deal with these challenges to ensure equitable and enabling learning.

Based on the passage, which of the following best illustrates a cause-and-effect relationship?

options.text: The use of technology-driven tools has led to more personalised learning experiences
Traditional teaching methods have remained unchanged despite technological advancements.
Technology in education has no significant effect on accessibility and engagement.
Digital distractions have no impact on students’ ability to focus in a tech-driven classroom.

questions.questionText:
On July 20, 1969, Neil Armstrong took mankind’s first step on the lunar surface, uttering the now-iconic words, “That’s one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind.” The Apollo 11 mission, executed by NASA, was hailed as a triumph of scientific achievement, engineering precision, and collective will. It marked a historic breakthrough not only for space exploration but also for humanity’s belief in pushing the boundaries of possibility.

Yet beneath the surface of celebration, the moon landing was deeply entangled in the geopolitical fabric of the Cold War. The U.S. space race against the Soviet Union had less to do with science and more to do with proving ideological superiority. The mission was as much a political performance as it was a scientific one, with the lunar flag and broadcast symbolising American dominance on a global stage.

Which of the following best supports the idea that the moon landing was more a political act than a scientific achievement?

options.text: The mission involved groundbreaking lunar research and the return of moon rock samples.
The globally broadcast event emphasised American presence and identity on lunar soil.
The mission sparked international space collaboration in the decades that followed.
Armstrong’s declaration aimed to unite humanity through a shared achievement.

questions.questionText:
The transatlantic slave trade, which lasted from the 16th to the 19th century, forcibly transported millions of Africans to the Americas. While often condemned today for its brutal inhumanity, at the time, it was defended by many European powers as an economic necessity. Proponents argued that the trade fuelled the growth of industries such as sugar, cotton, and tobacco, creating wealth for empires and providing labour for expanding colonial economies. 

Opponents, however, viewed the practice as a moral atrocity, emphasising the dehumanisation, violence, and generational trauma it inflicted on African communities. Over time, abolitionist movements across Europe and the Americas challenged the economic justification, asserting that ethical responsibility must outweigh financial interests. The eventual dismantling of the trade reflected a growing recognition that no economic benefit could justify systemic human suffering. However, the legacy of the slave trade, visible in persistent racial inequalities and cultural dislocation, remains a deeply embedded part of global history.

Which option best demonstrates a nuanced understanding of both the supporting and opposing arguments surrounding the transatlantic slave trade as discussed in the passage?

options.text:
Supporting Argument: The slave trade was essential for industrial progress and should be considered a necessary historical phase.
Opposing Argument: Modern economies would have developed without slavery, rendering it historically irrelevant.

Supporting Argument: The trade was seen as economically advantageous by colonial powers due to the labour it supplied.
Opposing Argument: Abolitionists argued that ethical values should take precedence over financial profit.

Supporting Argument: European nations used the slave trade to civilise underdeveloped societies through forced labour.
Opposing Argument: The slave trade was ineffective in producing real economic growth for anyone involved.

Supporting Argument: The moral critique of slavery began only after it ended, proving it had long-lasting acceptance.
Opposing Argument: African societies benefited from their interactions with European traders.

questions.questionText:
Cognitive literature, as an example, examines how human beings’ process information, make selections, and form memories. Behavioural psychology, stimulated via researchers like B.F. Skinner, makes a speciality of observable moves and how they're formed by using external reinforcements.

Psychoanalytic literature, rooted in the works of Sigmund Freud, researches into the unconscious, emphasising the function of adolescence and hidden goals in shaping personality. On the other hand, humanistic psychology, championed by figures like Carl Rogers, prioritises self-actualisation, inherent growth, and emotional well-being over deterministic views of conduct.

More modern-day psychological literature integrates neuroscientific findings, cultural views, and social dynamics, reflecting the evolving nature of mental inquiry. While these procedures fluctuate, they share a not unusual aim: to understand and interpret the human psyche, supplying deeper insights into private and societal improvement.

Based on this, which of the following most accurately reflects why psychology as a discipline must continuously adapt and refine its literature?

options.text: The complexity of human cognition and behaviour cannot be fully understood through a single theoretical lens, requiring an ongoing synthesis of emerging perspectives, empirical research, and interdisciplinary insights.
While older psychological theories retain their foundational value, new discoveries primarily serve to reinforce pre-existing frameworks rather than introduce novel paradigms or methodologies.

The rapid advancement of neuroscience and technology has rendered many classical psychological theories obsolete, necessitating a complete departure from historical frameworks in favour of biologically driven explanations.
Psychological literature remains largely static, but external factors such as cultural shifts and technological advancements occasionally require reinterpretation of its core principles.

questions.questionText:
Swami Vivekananda, an Indian spiritual leader and philosopher, emphasised the importance of self-realisation, universal brotherhood, and service to humanity. His teachings advocated for a balanced life that integrated spiritual growth with social responsibility. He believed that education should build character, strengthen the mind, and develop the capacity to face life’s challenges with confidence. Vivekananda's message resonated across boundaries, inspiring millions to embrace the idea of unity in diversity and inner strength. 

He consistently urged the youth to believe in themselves and to work not just for personal gain but for the upliftment of society at large. His words, such as “Arise, awake, and stop not till the goal is reached,” remain a powerful call to action even today.

Which of the following best supports the central ideas expressed in the passage?

options.text: True education is about scoring high marks to achieve financial security and fame.
Social change begins when individuals prioritise self-interest over community service.
Youth must channel their potential toward societal good, rooted in self-belief and moral strength.
Spiritual pursuits must be separated from practical life in order to maintain focus.

questions.questionText:
Health isn't always simply the absence of ailment; it's a dynamic state of physical, mental, and social well-being. Surprisingly, many small habits have a considerable effect on our health. For example, studies have shown that giggling can enhance blood flow and reduce stress hormones while drinking enough water can dramatically improve awareness.

Sleep, frequently unnoticed, is the other pillar of fitness. Chronic sleep deprivation is linked not just to fatigue but also to weakened immunity, weight gain, and even coronary heart disease. Meanwhile, mental health has increasingly been identified to be just as important as physical fitness. Practices like mindfulness and normal social interplay have been connected to lower rates of despair and tension.

Despite these insights, there's an ongoing debate about how much control people have over their health. While life choices are essential, genetics, environmental elements, and access to healthcare all play significant roles. Recognising this balance is essential to developing a practical and compassionate approach to public health.


Which of the following pairs best represents one supporting and one opposing argument related to the idea that ‘individual lifestyle choices are the main factor in determining health’?

options.text:
Supporting: Healthy habits like laughter and hydration can improve mental and physical well-being.
Opposing: People are fully responsible for their health, regardless of circumstances

Supporting: Sleep, nutrition, and mindfulness are proven to reduce disease risk.
Opposing: Health is entirely determined by genetics and cannot be changed by behaviour.

Supporting: Everyday actions like exercise and stress reduction significantly impact overall health.
Opposing: External factors such as environment and access to healthcare also shape health outcomes.

Supporting: Lack of sleep directly causes weight gain and poor immunity.
Opposing: Good health only depends on medical intervention, not personal habits.

questions.questionText:
Goal-seeking behaviour is a fundamental aspect of human motivation. It involves the conscious effort to set, pursue, and achieve specific objectives, whether personal, academic, or professional. While goals provide direction and purpose, the way individuals approach them can vary greatly. Some rely on structured planning and persistent effort, while others are driven by intrinsic passion or external rewards. Psychological studies suggest that clarity of goals, feedback mechanisms, and a sense of autonomy significantly enhance goal achievement. 
However, blindly chasing goals without reflection can sometimes lead to burnout or ethical compromises. Thus, effective goal pursuit is not just about reaching outcomes but also maintaining balance, adaptability, and self-awareness along the journey. 
Based on the passage, what can be inferred about the most sustainable approach to achieving goals?

options.text: Pursuing goals with a strong focus on end results, even if it demands sacrificing well-being.
Maintaining flexibility and ethical reflection throughout the goal pursuit process.
Relying on external rewards and structured routines to drive consistent goal success.
Committing to a fixed goal path early on to avoid distractions and ambiguity.

questions.questionText:
Passage:

The concept of free will has long been explored in philosophy, psychology, and science. Two major perspectives in this discussion are determinism and libertarianism. Determinism suggests that human actions and decisions may be influenced by prior conditions such as genetics, environment, and past experiences. From this viewpoint, choices appear to follow patterns that can be understood as part of a continuous chain of events.

On the other hand, libertarianism emphasises the ability of individuals to make choices independently. This perspective focuses on personal agency and the belief that people can act freely, even when influenced by external factors. It highlights the importance of autonomy and the human capacity for reflection and decision-making.

Which of the following statements reflects the determinist perspective on decision-making?

options.text: People make decisions without any influence from past events.
Each choice is shaped by previous experiences and conditions.
Individuals always act spontaneously and independently.
Human actions are entirely unpredictable and random.

questions.questionText:
Antioxidants are molecules that help protect the body’s cells from damage caused by free radicals—unstable compounds that can harm cells and contribute to ageing and diseases like cancer. Common antioxidants include vitamins C and E, selenium, and beta-carotene, which are found in many fruits, vegetables, nuts, and grains. The idea that antioxidants can prevent serious diseases has made them popular in health and nutrition discussions. Some studies suggest that diets rich in antioxidant-containing foods are linked to lower risks of certain chronic illnesses, including heart disease and cancer. 

However, other research has shown that taking antioxidant supplements does not always produce the same benefits and may even have negative effects in high doses. While antioxidants from whole foods can support overall health, scientists caution against relying on supplements as a guaranteed way to prevent disease. Therefore, while antioxidants play an important role in protecting the body, their ability to prevent complex diseases like cancer is still not fully proven and may depend on how they are consumed.

Based on the passage, which of the following best demonstrates a nuanced cause-and-effect relationship between antioxidants and disease prevention?

options.text: The body produces free radicals as a result of antioxidant deficiency, which directly causes cancer.
Antioxidants eliminate all health risks by neutralising every free radical in the body.
Consumption of antioxidant-rich foods may reduce disease risk due to their natural ability to combat cellular damage, although supplements may not have the same effect.
High doses of antioxidants cure cancer by reversing all cell mutations caused by free radicals.

questions.questionText:
Cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) is a widely used psychological treatment that helps individuals identify and modify negative thought patterns. Studies have demonstrated that CBT is highly effective in treating anxiety, depression and other mental health disorders. By encouraging patients to develop healthier coping mechanisms, this therapy fostered resilience and improves overall well-being. Additionally, therapists employ structured techniques to guide patients towards positive behavioural changes, making CBT one of the most evidence-based approaches in modern psychology.

 

Identify the error and select the correct usage based on the passage.

options.text:
Error: The use of the verb ‘fostered’ is incorrect. 
Correct Usage: Replace ‘fostered’ with ‘fosters’.

Error: The use of the word ‘Additionally’ is inaccurate. 
Correct Usage: Replace ‘Additionally’ with ‘In contrast’.

Error: The word ‘structured’ in ‘structured techniques’ is unnecessary.
Correct Usage: ‘Therapists employ techniques to guide patients’
No error in the passage; it is correct as written.

questions.questionText:
In most compelling stories, character development is at the heart of narrative progression. Characters often begin their journey shaped by personal flaws, limited perspectives, or specific life circumstances. As the plot unfolds, these individuals are tested through conflicts, relationships, and life-altering events that challenge their beliefs and behaviour. For instance, a timid protagonist may gradually gain confidence by confronting their fears, or a morally ambiguous figure may evolve into a more principled character after witnessing injustice.

The development is not always linear; characters may relapse, question themselves, or even regress before moving forward. This complexity adds realism and emotional depth, allowing readers to connect with their struggles and triumphs. Relationships with other characters also play a key role, as allies and antagonists alike can act as mirrors or catalysts for transformation. A well-developed character will show internal change by the story’s end, whether it’s growth, realisation, or even tragic downfall, making the narrative not just a sequence of events, but a profound exploration of human nature.

Which of the following best explains a cause-and-effect relationship described in the passage?

options.text: Characters start as flawless individuals, which makes their development less impactful.
Relationships with others cause characters to remain stagnant and unchanging.
Exposure to conflict and challenges causes characters to undergo internal transformation.
The end of the story causes the characters to lose their identity and purpose.

questions.questionText:
The discovery of penicillin by Alexander Fleming in 1928 revolutionised medicine, leading to the development of antibiotics that could effectively treat bacterial infections. Before this breakthrough, minor infections often proved fatal, and there were limited treatment options for diseases such as pneumonia and strep throat. The mass production of penicillin during World War II saved countless lives and marked the beginning of the antibiotic era. However, the overuse of antibiotics in modern times has led to the rise of antibiotic-resistant bacteria, posing a significant challenge to global health. Scientists continue to research new antimicrobial solutions to combat this growing threat.

What best describes the tone of the passage?

In today’s fast-paced world, multitasking is often praised as a valuable skill, especially among students and professionals trying to balance multiple responsibilities. However, cognitive research suggests that multitasking may not be as effective as commonly believed, particularly when it comes to learning and memory retention. Studies have shown that the human brain is not truly capable of focusing on multiple complex tasks at once. Instead, it rapidly switches attention from one task to another, resulting in divided focus and decreased efficiency.

When learners try to study while texting, watching videos, or browsing social media, their ability to process and retain information declines. This constant shifting of attention can lead to cognitive overload and shallow understanding. While it may feel productive, multitasking often results in longer completion times and more errors. Therefore, many educators and psychologists argue that focused, single-task learning is far more efficient and beneficial for deep comprehension and long-term retention. The belief in multitasking as a learning booster, they argue, may be more myth than reality.

Which of the following best summarises the central argument of the passage “Is Multitasking a Myth in Learning Efficiency?”

options.text: Multitasking is an essential skill in modern life, and students should be trained to handle multiple tasks at once for academic success.
While multitasking appears efficient, research shows it reduces learning effectiveness by dividing attention and overloading the brain.
The human brain can adapt to multitasking over time, making it a useful tool for learning and working in high-pressure environments.
Multitasking enhances memory and comprehension only when used alongside digital tools like videos and educational apps.

questions.questionText:
The end of the monarchy in France was not merely the result of a single event but the culmination of deepening crises layered across decades. The rigid structure of the Ancient Régime had long placed privilege in the hands of a narrow aristocracy, while the majority languished under oppressive taxation and limited rights. Intellectual ferment sparked by Enlightenment thinkers like Rousseau and Voltaire questioned the very legitimacy of divine-right rule, igniting philosophical unrest among the emerging bourgeoisie and disillusioned lower classes.

However, the monarchy might have withstood ideological dissent had it not been for the mounting economic turmoil. War debts, food scarcity, and skyrocketing bread prices bred desperation. King Louis XVI’s indecisiveness and failure to enact meaningful reforms alienated both moderates and radicals. The convening of the Estates-General in 1789, meant to offer solutions, instead exposed the deep fissures within French society. Popular anger spilt into the streets, culminating in the storming of the Bastille—a symbolic rejection of tyranny.

As revolutionary fervour spread, the monarchy’s authority eroded rapidly. The eventual execution of Louis XVI in 1793 was less an isolated act of defiance than the logical consequence of years of injustice, disconnection, and failed adaptation. The end of the monarchy in France was thus not accidental; it was the inevitable effect of a system unable or unwilling to evolve.

Which statement most accurately reflects a complex cause-and-effect relationship underlying the collapse of the French monarchy, as inferred from the passage?

options.text: The monarchy’s reliance on divine right and suppression of reform ignited a chain of intellectual dissent that directly culminated in the king’s execution.
The convergence of economic hardship, political inertia, and philosophical awakening catalysed a revolutionary shift that dismantled monarchical rule.
Revolutionary leaders exploited Enlightenment rhetoric to manufacture unrest, thereby orchestrating the monarchy’s fall for political gain.
Foreign wars and external debts overshadowed domestic discontent, forcing the monarchy to dissolve under international pressure.

questions.questionText:
The ancient event of Samudra Manthan, or the Churning of the Ocean, symbolises a deeper philosophical truth of human life. According to it, gods and demons collaborated to churn the cosmic ocean to attain the nectar of immortality. However, before the nectar emerged, the ocean first released a deadly poison. Lord Shiva selflessly absorbed the poison to save others, turning his throat blue, earning him the name Neelkanth.

Philosophically, it was a journey of life and self-awareness. The ocean represents the thoughts, and the churning symbolises the struggles amongst good and evil inside ourselves. The poison signifies the unavoidable struggle one needs to go through before attaining enlightenment, symbolised by the nectar. Shiva’s act embodies the concept that self-sacrifice and internal strength are crucial to overcome adversity. Thus, the myth illustrates that profound rewards, like information or liberation, emerge only after enduring difficulty and chaotic events.

In light of the above, which of the following best represents the cause-and-effect relationship derived from the philosophical interpretation in the passage?

options.text: The ocean produced poison first because the gods and demons lacked unity in their efforts.
Shiva consumed the poison to assert his superiority over both gods and demons.
The emergence of poison before nectar symbolises that hardship and suffering often precede wisdom and enlightenment
The gods and demons churned the ocean to create chaos and test Shiva’s strength.

questions.questionText:
London, with its blend of historical grandeur and contemporary flair, has long been a magnet for travellers from across the globe. From the regal majesty of Buckingham Palace to the modern spectacle of the London Eye, the city seamlessly bridges past and present. Its diverse neighbourhoods, each with unique cultural flavours, offer something for every type of visitor. Yet, London’s appeal goes beyond its attractions; it lies in the experience it provides. 
Whether navigating its world-class transport, strolling through Hyde Park, or discovering street art in Shoreditch, tourists often find themselves immersed in both local charm and global influence. This rich layering of heritage, innovation, and inclusivity makes London not just a place to visit, but one to remember. 
Based on the passage, what can be inferred about the kind of experience London offers to tourists?

options.text: A transformative journey that connects individuals with both cultural depth and cosmopolitan energy.
A predictable tour of iconic sites without significant engagement with modern urban life.
A limited experience focused more on aesthetics than on interactive cultural immersion.
A rushed exploration driven by a checklist of historical monuments and royal attractions.

questions.questionText:
Physicians undertake varying strategies to impart medical facts to patients, formed by using cultural context, personal touches, and scientific training. In Western International locations, many medical doctors follow a patient-targeted method, emphasising transparency, shared decision-making, and empathetic communication. They regularly use visual aids, simplified language, and open-ended inquiries to make sure their patients understand.

In comparison, physicians in more hierarchical or conventional structures, which include regions of Asia or the Middle East might also depend upon authoritative verbal exchange, in which the medical doctor affords direct commands and the patient listens without tons questioning. This approach can create readability and self-assurance, in particular in time-sensitive or emergency settings, but may also limit patient engagement in long-term care.

Some doctors integrate both models, tailoring their strategies to shape the patient’s background and emotional needs. As healthcare becomes more globalised, knowledge and the ability to adapt to numerous communication styles have become essential for effective treatment and patient satisfaction.

What is the tone of the passage?

options.text: Critical – highlighting the flaws in how physicians communicate globally.
Persuasive – urging all physicians to adopt a specific communication method.
Casual – using informal language to discuss medical communication practices.
Objective – presenting a balanced comparison of different physician communication techniques.
